subcategory: KG-RAG subgraph retrieval trained with graph-theoretic pseudo-labels
task: Multi-hop knowledge-graph question answering (KGQA) with LLM generation
problem: Subgraph retrieval for KG-RAG relies on heuristic shortest paths or multi-hop traversal, giving incomplete, semantically drifting subgraphs that ignore how the LLM uses fine-grained structure.
architecture: DCTR: (1) DCFGR builds compact and complete pseudo-label subgraphs via maximum-flow retrieval and a dual-flux path extractor (MaxMin-InfoPath lower bound + MaxDensity-InfoPath upper bound); (2) DSRS converts the discrete pseudo-labels into a differentiable surrogate so the retriever's ranking is trained to highlight salient triples; retrieved subgraph is passed to an LLM for answering.
retriever: trainable triple retriever initialised with GTE embeddings
key_results: WebQSP retrieval: path recall 0.890, GPT-4o triple recall 0.866, answer recall 0.956 vs 0.857/0.815/0.923 for SubgraphRAG.
CWQ retrieval: 0.829/0.839/0.928 vs 0.801/0.807/0.914 for SubgraphRAG, at similar retrieval time (12 s).
Relative improvement in GPT-4o triple recall over SubgraphRAG of 5.1% on WebQSP and 3.2% on CWQ.
strengths: Principled pseudo-label construction with theoretical motivation; cross-dataset transfer (CWQ to WebQSP and back) is reported.
Averaged over five seeds; ablations for both retrieval and generation stages.

limitations.text: Evaluated only on two Freebase KGQA benchmarks.
Pseudo-labels require answer entities at training time (inference is answer-free).

title: DCTR: Dual-Constraint Subgraph Optimization for Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation
